   ‘How is it possible?’: Students in Kalimantan protest against Indonesian haze
 Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
 A protest outside the Central Kalimantan Governor’s office in Palangkaraya, Indonesia, on Oct 23, demanding action over forest and land fires.
 PHOTO: AFP
 Published   Oct 24, 2026, 01:35 PM
 Updated   Oct 24, 2026, 02:05 PM
 Set as preferred source Listen Palangkaraya , Indonesia – Hundreds of students protested late on Oct 23 in Indonesia’s Palangkaraya, demanding the government do more to tackle a wildfire crisis that has shrouded their city and the wider region in toxic haze for months.
 The students, many wearing surgical masks, gathered under an eerily orange sky amid severely reduced visibility and waved banners urging the authorities to declare a national emergency to free up more aid.
 “The officials are morons, yet they get fantastic perks while the lives of the common people are tragic,” read one protest placard nailed to a wall outside the office of the governor of Central Kalimantan – an Indonesian province on the island of Borneo where the fires are taking place.
 The demonstrators sang the patriotic song ‘Indonesia Pusaka’ and engaged in light skirmishes with police.
 No injuries or arrests were reported. As night fell, the protesters cleared up their trash before dispersing peacefully.
 “We call upon the Central Kalimantan provincial government to state clearly that it is unable to mitigate this disaster, so that the situation may be officially designated a national disaster,” protest leader Yuyun Sanjaya told the crowd.
 “How is it possible that such thick, dense smoke is being inhaled by helpless elderly people and newborn infants, and the government simply lets it happen?”
 Wildfires have burnt more than 1.9 million ha in the nine months to September, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas – a figure the government has not confirmed or denied.
 The resulting haze has sickened hundreds of thousands in Indonesia and reached as far as Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor.
 Amid diplomatic objections from neighbouring countries, patience has also been running thin at home, with sporadic anti-government protests.
 On Oct 22, Indonesian schoolchildren prayed for rain on the island of Java, where fires have also ravaged several regencies and conservation areas. AFP
